Content:
Box models are powerful because they provide a general method for dividing large numbers. And, as we've seen, they can also handle cases with remainders.

Content:
Let's consider the following three-digit by one-digit division problem.

Content:
[MATH: 630 \div 3]

Content:
We set up our box model in the usual way.

Content:
| | | | |
| | [MATH: 3] | | | | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 0] | | | | |

Content:
We now follow our usual four steps:

Content:
Step 1: Pick a (fairly large) multiple of [MATH: 3] that is easy to compute but is no larger than [MATH: 630.] Let's pick [MATH: 3 \times {\color{blue}200} = 600.]

Content:
We write [MATH: {\color{blue}200}] on top of the box and subtract [MATH: 3 \times{\color{blue}200}] from [MATH: 630] inside the box.

Content:
| | [MATH: \color{blue}200] | |
| | [MATH: 3] | | | | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 0] | | / | [MATH: -\!] | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 0] | | / | | | [MATH: \color{red}3] | [MATH: \color{red}0] | | | | |

Content:
Step 2: Next, we bring [MATH: {\color{red}30}] to the right.

Content:
| | [MATH: 200] | |
| | [MATH: 3] | | | | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 0] | | / | [MATH: -\!] | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 0] | | / | | | [MATH: \color{red}3] | [MATH: \color{red}0] | | | | | [MATH: \color{red}3] | [MATH: \color{red}0] | | | |

Content:
Step 3: Pick a multiple of [MATH: 3] that is easy to compute but is no larger than [MATH: 30.] Let's pick [MATH: 3 \times {\color{blue}10} = 30.]

Content:
We write [MATH: \color{blue}10] above the box and subtract [MATH: 3 \times {\color{blue}10}] from [MATH: \color{red}30] inside the box.

Content:
| | [MATH: 200] | [MATH: \color{blue}10] |
| | [MATH: 3] | | | | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 0] | | / | [MATH: -\!] | [MATH: 6] | [MATH: 0] | [MATH: 0] | | / | | | [MATH: \color{red}3] | [MATH: \color{red}0] | | | | | [MATH: \color{red}3] | [MATH: \color{red}0] | | / | [MATH: -\!] | [MATH: 3] | [MATH: 0] | | / | | | [MATH: \fbox{0}] | | | |

Content:
We get [MATH: \fbox{0},] so the division is done.

Content:
Step 4: To find the quotient of [MATH: 630 \div 3,] we add the numbers on top of the boxes:
[MATH: 200+10=210]

Content:
Therefore,
[MATH: 630 \div 3 = 210.]
